text:
elena: Heads-up — Acme integration started failing after we swapped them to model=rwinf/llama4b-v3-quant a few hours ago. They see invalid JSON / missing top-level keys when using structured_output=json. Customer report attached.

support-bot: Ticket #45321 created for AcmeCorp (priority: P2).

elena: Example response from the customer (copied):
```json
{
  "order_id": 12345,
  "items": [
    {"sku": "X-100", "qty": 2}
  ],
  "shipping": {"method": "ground"}
  ...
}
```
Customer says their parser throws `Unexpected end of JSON input`. They also report that sometimes the `discounts` and `metadata` keys are just missing (previously always present, possibly null).

elena: Repro steps I used (from support environment):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwinf/llama4b-v3-quant","input":"Generate order JSON for order #12345","structured_output":true,"stream":true}'
```
Response stream shows chunks but final assembled payload is truncated ~30% of the time. If I set `stream:false` the output is well-formed.

kai: Thanks — tagging eng-ml. Quick Qs: which quant config (8-bit/4-bit) and is this happening for both streaming and non-streaming for them? Also any proxy/ingress that might truncate streams?

elena: Customer is on our hosted API (no private proxy). They said streaming=true for their client. They saw both parse errors and dropped keys. We verified with quant=4bit and quant=8bit (they tried both), issue present in both but more frequent with 4bit.

viktor: eng-sre check: can you paste request IDs and a sample request_ts? I want to check Nginx/edge logs for truncated connections. Also which runtime revision was the canary pinned to?

elena: Request IDs: req_0a7f3b9a, req_0a7f4c2d, req_0a7f5d33 (sample). Canary rollout note: llama4b-v3-quant was rolled at 2026-02-18 04:12 UTC on serving-runtime rev rrt-20260218-3.

kai: I pulled a repro locally using the same model and `stream=true` + sequence length ~512. I can reproduce the truncated final JSON in ~25% of runs. Hypothesis: a new streaming flush in the tokenizer/serializer path emits a trailing partial object boundary, and the post-processor that wraps the structured output sometimes drops keys that were emitted in earlier chunks when merging chunked JSON.

kai: Quick mitigation: request the customer to set `stream=false` or pin model to rwinf/llama4b-v2 while we fix. I can prepare a hotfix to the serializer that ensures chunk boundaries emit complete JSON frames.

sam: If we push a hotfix, what's the expected SLA to roll to hosted? Need to coordinate customer comms (they're revenue-impacting).

kai: If we hotfix the serializer in the canary binary and run a quick canary re-check, I can have a rollback/hotfix deploy within ~30–45 minutes. Will need SRE to approve a fast track.

viktor: I can fast-track the canary patch and monitor health. Please include the failing request ids and enable verbose chunk logs for those requests. I'll also tail the edge to confirm no TCP resets.

elena: Sent request ids and enabled debug on the customer org. Customer is willing to accept pin-to-previous-model for now but prefers a fix.

kai: Root cause (prelim): a change in the post-processing serializer (rrt-20260218-3) switches to an incremental merge that assumed chunk atomicity. For certain tokenization boundaries the incremental merge would drop keys that were only present in early chunks when encountering a partial closing token. Essentially we were letting partial frames mutate the accumulator.

kai: Plan: (1) hotfix serializer to avoid mutating accumulator on partial frames and always complete object boundaries before merge; (2) re-run the canary tests with streaming=true and seq_len up to 1024; (3) push if green.

elena: Workaround communicated to Acme: pin to model=rwinf/llama4b-v2 OR set `stream:false`. They accepted the pin for now.

support-bot: Update on Ticket #45321: workaround applied (model pin), engineering investigating.

viktor: Deployed serializer hotfix to canary and running integration checks now. Will post results in ~20m.

kai: Integration checks passed for 100/100 runs at seq_len=1024 with streaming=true. No truncation, keys preserved. Planning staged rollout.

sam: I'll prepare customer-facing note explaining root cause and ETA for full rollout. Keep me posted on rollback window.

elena: I'll update Acme and ask them to validate the canary patch next hour; keeping case open until they confirm.

kai: After rollout we'll add an automated structured-output test to our canary suite (streaming + quant permutations) to prevent regressions.

elena: Thanks all — marking ticket P2 -> monitoring.
